title: SLO sync lab: capacity scenarios, stakeholder syncs, and pilot playbook
body:
Purpose:
Set up a lightweight, repeatable "SLO Sync Lab" series to align product, platform, infra, and CS on SLOs and reliability interventions. The focus for this tranche is: capacity scenario modeling, telemetry gaps, and a pilot runbook that teams can borrow.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: model-serving inference endpoints (hosted + dedicated), queueing/backpressure surfaces, autoscaling behavior, and per-route SLOs.
- Out of scope: full org-wide SLA contract language, billing changes, or product pricing decisions (we'll surface implications but won't decide pricing here).

High-level goals (6-week experiment window):
1) Produce 3 capacity scenarios (nominal, degraded, recovery) with expected error/latency impact to SLOs.
2) Create an SLI mapping table for the top 8 services that contribute >90% of 95th p99 latency risk.
3) Run two cross-functional table-top workshops and one hands-on chaos-lite sim.
4) Deliver a pilot playbook (rollout + rollback + communications) and a short README for feature teams.

Success criteria (how we know it's useful):
- Teams can run the scenario model locally and get a grounded estimate for error budget burn within 1 hour.
- Observability gaps identified (metric missing or stale) reduced from 12 -> <=4 for pilot services.
- One feature team signs up to use the playbook in next feature launch (signoff by product lead).

Why this is different from other SLO work: 
- Emphasis on capacity-driven scenarios (not just threshold tuning).
- Lightweight labs to force tradeoffs and stakeholder alignment, not another policy doc.

Planned artifacts to deliver:
- 3 scenario sheets (CSV-friendly) and a worked example notebook (python/pseudo).
- SLI mapping table with source, collection frequency, owner, and remediation recipe.
- Pilot playbook: checklist + runbook + stakeholder contact list + template emails.
- Telemetry gap report with prioritized TODOs.

6-week schedule (high level):
Week 0 (prep, owner): Priya - collect baseline metrics, invite stakeholders, create scenario templates.
Week 1: Workshop #1 (table-top): align definitions, confirm top services, and introduce scenarios.
Week 2: Instrumentation sprint: teams fix highest priority telemetry gaps (2-day focus).
Week 3: Scenario modeling and dry run (internal): produce burn projections for each scenario.
Week 4: Chaos-lite sim (limited scope, 1-hour blast for one service), Workshop #2 (review results).
Week 5: Draft pilot playbook and onboarding checklist.
Week 6: Pilot signups + retro + next-step decision (scale, pause, refactor).

Sample workshop agendas (table-top):
- 10m: purpose + success criteria + roll call
- 15m: quick metrics baseline (what's the current 95th/99th and error rate curve)
- 30m: scenario walk-through (nominal / degraded / recovery) and impact mapping
- 20m: decide mitigations (caching, prefix-KV, model variant fallback, routing policy)
- 15m: actions & owners + follow-up commitments

Roles & RACI (draft):
- Sponsor: Lina Barrett (VP SRE) - approve scope and staffing runway.
- Program Owner: Priya Rao - coordinate, deliver artifacts, run workshops.
- Observability: Evan Kim - lead telemetry gap triage and dashboards.
- Serving Runtime SME: Tomás Ortega - lead scenario modeling for model-serving specifics.
- Product Representative(s): Marisol Vega - validate customer impact framing and sign off pilots.
- Engineering Liaisons: per-team SRE/owner (TBD in workshop).

Telemetry & SLI mapping (short example rows - full table attached in artifacts):
- route/renderer.generate.token-latency_p95 -> collected in traces -> 10s resolution -> owner: serving-runtime -> remediation: rate limit/batching profile change
- route/embed.encode.error_rate -> exported by api-gateway -> 1m -> owner: platform-api -> remediation: fallback to cheaper quantized model
Notes: if metric TTL >10m or delayed, mark as gap and add to instrumentation sprint.

Capacity scenarios (worked examples):
1) Nominal (steady-state): normal traffic distribution, autoscaler healthy. Expectation: p95 within target, error budget usage low.
2) Degraded (loss of a subset of GPUs / AZ): traffic shifts, increased queueing; model-fallback starts at 10% of requests, p95 spikes by 2-3x. Use this to test graceful fallback thresholds.
3) Recovery (post-incident ramp): aggressive traffic surge as backlog drains; autoscaling may oscillate. Evaluate safety net (circuit breaker + fallback) and error budget burn during ramp.
- For each scenario include: input assumptions, expected metrics, mitigation knobs, rollback triggers (quantitative).

Pilot playbook (outline):
- Pre-launch checklist: SLI dashboard available, alert rules + runbook linked, owner assigned, canary route defined.
- Launch steps: enable canary 5% traffic -> monitor 30m -> increase stepwise if safe.
- Rollback triggers: sustained 5-minute p95 > threshold AND error-rate doubling for >5m.
- Postmortem trigger: if error budget burn >30% in 24h.
- Communications: slack channel template, customer-facing status snippet, stakeholder on-call list.

Risk & mitigations (quick list):
- Risk: Observability gaps take longer than expected -> Mitigation: narrow scope to 3 metrics for first pass and use sampling.
- Risk: Autoscaler behaviour not reproducible locally -> Mitigation: run a short cluster-level sim with the infra team and capture parameters.
- Risk: Teams overloaded -> Mitigation: embed a 2-day instrumentation SWAT (SREs + platform engineers).

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Is there budget for a small burst of dedicated GPUs for the chaos sim? (ask infra finance) -> ACTION: Priya to ping infra-finance (Jira REL-412)
- Do we need legal sign-off for customer-facing status language? likely no for pilot but check.
- Which feature team is the easiest early adopter? product to nominate during workshop.

Next steps (this week):
- Create the scenario CSV templates and upload to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/REL/SLO+Sync+Lab (linked artifact above).
- Schedule Workshop #1: 60 minutes + pre-read email to all invitees.
- Spin up an observability quick dashboard (Evan) with the 8 baseline SLIs.

Quick checklist for invites & pre-reads:
- Pre-read: one-page baseline metrics (p95/p99/error-rate) for your service
- Bring: primary SRE/owner and someone who can speak to current autoscaler config
- Expectation: commit to 2 days of focused instrumentation work if invited

Appendix (working links & rough templates):
- Template email: "FYI: SLO Sync Lab Workshop #1 — please bring baseline metrics" (copy in Confluence)
- Scenario CSV: columns = scenario_name, service, assumption, expected_p95, expected_error_rate, mitigation_1, mitigation_2, rollback_trigger

Raw scratch notes (informal):
- Keep friction low. Teams hate docs that ask for 20 charts. Ask for the minimum: p95/p99 + error-rate + one traffic profile sample.
- If we can show an immediate quick win (one alarm removed or one gap closed) we'll get momentum.
